title: Business website and enquiry workflow
summary: How a service business can turn scattered enquiries into one tracked, mobile-friendly workflow — and how the outcome would be measured.
problem: A service business receives enquiries through multiple channels and has no consistent record of follow-up.
assessment: Map enquiry sources, response ownership, required information and the points where prospective customers are lost.
solution: A responsive service website, structured contact form, clear service pages and a documented lead follow-up workflow.
implementation: Define the content and form fields, validate submissions, route enquiries to a responsible contact, and test mobile accessibility and confirmation messages.
results: No client result is claimed. A real engagement would report measured response time, qualified enquiries and conversion against a recorded baseline.
technology: Responsive web development, form validation, analytics configured with consent, and CRM integration where selected.

metrics.name: Enquiry response time
metrics.why: Shows whether prospective customers are followed up promptly.
metrics.how: Time from an enquiry being received to the first reply, taken from timestamps in the enquiry record.

metrics.name: Qualified enquiries
metrics.how: Monthly count of enquiries that meet criteria agreed with the business before launch.

metrics.name: Conversion rate
metrics.why: Shows whether the website turns visits into enquiries.
metrics.how: Visitors-to-enquiries from consent-based analytics, compared with a baseline recorded before launch.

metrics.name: Form completion rate
metrics.why: Reveals form fields or steps that put people off.
metrics.how: Started versus submitted forms, reviewed alongside mobile and desktop usage.

title: Small-business e-commerce foundation
summary: A planning view of taking a small retailer online: catalogue, payments, delivery and returns defined as one process before launch.
problem: A retailer wants to sell online but product information, stock updates, payments and delivery steps are not documented in one process.
assessment: Review catalogue quality, inventory ownership, payment settlement, delivery coverage, returns and customer support.
solution: A mobile-friendly product catalogue and checkout connected to a defined order fulfilment process.
implementation: Prepare product data, configure a suitable payment provider, test successful and failed payments, and document fulfilment and refund handling.
results: No sales uplift or conversion figure is asserted. Performance should be measured after launch using order completion, fulfilment time, cancellation and support data.
technology: E-commerce storefront, payment-provider integration, order records and analytics.

metrics.name: Order completion rate
metrics.why: Shows how many started checkouts end in a paid order.
metrics.how: Completed orders divided by checkouts started, including failed-payment reasons.

metrics.name: Fulfilment time
metrics.why: Shows whether the delivery promise is being kept.
metrics.how: Time from payment confirmation to dispatch and to delivery, from order records.

metrics.name: Cancellations and returns
metrics.why: Points to product-information or delivery problems.
metrics.how: Cancelled and returned orders as a share of all orders, with the stated reason.

metrics.name: Support contacts per order
metrics.why: Shows where customers are confused or unsure.
metrics.how: Questions received per order, grouped by topic.

title: Administrative workflow automation
summary: A walk-through of replacing repeated copy-and-paste between forms, spreadsheets and email with one validated, trackable workflow.
problem: Staff repeatedly copy information between forms, spreadsheets and email, making hand-offs difficult to track.
assessment: Document the current process, data owners, approval steps, exceptions and baseline time per task.
solution: A validated intake form, centralised records, task notifications and a reviewable status workflow.
implementation: Pilot one workflow, test permissions and exception handling, train users and keep a manual fallback during rollout.
results: No time-saving percentage is claimed. Compare task duration, error rate and overdue work before and after deployment.
technology: Web forms, workflow automation, database records and role-based access.

metrics.name: Task duration
metrics.why: Shows whether the workflow really saves staff time.
metrics.how: Average time per task from the start of a request to completion, before and after rollout.

metrics.name: Error rate
metrics.why: Shows whether validation removes re-keying mistakes.
metrics.how: Records needing correction as a share of all records, from a sampled review.

metrics.name: Overdue work
metrics.why: Shows whether hand-offs are visible and acted on.
metrics.how: Count of tasks past their due date, taken from the status workflow.

metrics.name: Manual fallback use
metrics.why: Shows whether people trust the new process.
metrics.how: How often the manual fallback is used during and after the pilot.
